notes.title: A new Xeno threat emerges!
notes.content:
Hello Marines,

A new sci-fi game joins the Firesquid lineup:[b] Xenopurge[/b]!

With a very similar theme to USC, but a very different gameplay:
[list]
[*] Fight the alien threat
[*] Command and guide your troops
[*] Manage your soldiers and gears
[/list]
[h3]Check out the game and wishlist![/h3]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2983410/Xenopurge/

Xenopurge is a [b]real-time tactics game[/b] where you take the role of a commander, set up in a base of command, issuing orders remotely to your elite squad on the field. From several computer screens, you see the blueprints of the facilities your units traverse, directing them to search, recover, and destroy. Other than by your direct command, they will adapt to their surroundings, fending off the enemy in their sights.

The ever-present [b]Xeno alien threat[/b] permeates every mission. You and your team are a part of the organisation M.A.C.E (Mercer’s Advanced Combat Enterprises), tasked with purging the system of their presence in Xenowarfare. Recruit new members with a variety of skill specialties, upgrade their equipment, and improve your command tactics to achieve this goal, without losing too many of your people along the way.

In this [b]retro-futuristic military world[/b], the grit of warfare hangs heavy on your shoulders. [b]Alien horrors[/b] await around every door and corner for your squad. Do not hesitate to make your decisions, as failure means the alien infestation will consume everything.

notes.title: Play with friends during the Couch Coop Fest!
notes.content:
Hello Marines!

We're part of the Couch Coop Fest! Play great games with friends and family, including USC: Counterforce!

[h3]USC: Counterforce has this cool feature to play with your friends: Remote Play Together![/h3]

Gear up and take the fight to the enemy, but you don't have to do it alone. [b]Steam Remote Play Together allows you to invite a fellow marine to join your fight.[/b] You can play with up to two (you and your friend). One player owns and runs the game using the Remote Play Together feature to invite a friend.

[h3]How to Use Remote Play Together[/h3]
Here's a step-by-step guide to get you started:
Start by launching the game from your Steam library. Once you're in the game, open your Friend List on Steam. From there, send them an invitation to join your game: simply right-click on their name and select the "Invite to Remote Play Together" option. Your friend will receive the invitation and can accept it to join you. [b]You will be sharing and streaming the game for your friend.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/94b10d303f648abd346028dd62477f9a6a8abb2c.jpg[/img]
To better play USC: Counterforce using Remote Play Together, we recommend that you share your squad files with your friend. If you host the game, add their squad file in your squad folder here: %userprofile%\AppData\LocalLow\Angry Cat Studios\USC Counterforce\squads. You can choose the squads you wish to play with. Only the host will gain XP and get the unlocked items. Once the run ends and your team has won, give your friend's squad file back, so they can have the new statistics and materials stored in that squad file.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/4e1cb551b14c4327e115157a45fc087f6a284b54.png[/img]
[h3]Remote Play Together Features[/h3]
USC: Counterforce's “coop mode”, powered by Remote Play Together, offers some features to enhance your shared game experience:
[list]
[*] [b]Individual or shared controls[/b]: You and your friend can control the game using your own keyboards and mice. This means you can coordinate your tactics and strategies effectively. You can also share control of the keyboard and mouse. It's all about teamwork, and this feature allows you to truly work together.
[*] [b]Stream video, audio, and voice[/b]: Remote Play Together enables you to stream video, audio, and voice between players. This means you can communicate and strategize in real-time, just like you would if you were playing side-by-side.
[*] [b]Voice chat and game volume[/b]: All your voice chat and game volume options are conveniently available in one place, so you can fine-tune your settings to match your preferred style of play.
[/list]
Time to enlist your fellow friends, share the action, and prove that you deserve to be part of the Ultimate Space Commando. Get ready to lock and load, marines!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/0646620e7af37bc9744d2e3c152179beda703b2c.png[/img]

[h3]But what about online coop outside of Remote Play Together?[/h3]
USC: Counterforce is developed by a team of two developers. While including online coop outside of Remote Play Together would be interesting, it's essential to understand the limitations that led to this decision. Developing a coop mode adds a significant workload to setting up the architecture needed and would potentially delay the full release. Making a stable and enjoyable online coop mode is complex for many reasons. It involves synchronizing game states between multiple players, dealing with latency issues, and ensuring balanced gameplay. This complexity can lead to unforeseen technical challenges and require extensive testing and debugging which significantly increases the scope of QA and testing. Implementing an online coop feature requires a dedicated effort to create and maintain servers and grouping systems. The team needs to thoroughly test the game's server infrastructure and online interactions to ensure a smooth and bug-free experience for all. This process was time-consuming and resource-intensive, preventing us from working on the core features, polish, balance, and bug fixes.

Our goal is to make the best game possible. Choosing to rely on Remote Play Together is a practical choice. It allowed the team to concentrate their efforts on other aspects of the game and deliver a more polished and enjoyable experience for all, but [b]still allows you to play with friends[/b]!

The USC: Counterforce team

notes.title: Celebrating the Turn-based Carnival with a 50% discount!
notes.content:
[h3]USC: Counterforce is 50% off for the Turn-based Carnival![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/43f76c61874064e1115e3c92e1aecc4cb3e53f3a.png[/img]

To celebrate this very cool event, we're coming back on the turn-based mechanics of the game.

[h3]Let's talk about two turn based games that inspired us for USC: Counterforce. From the 1990s, learn more about: [b]Incubation: Time Is Running Out (1997)[/b] and [b]Gorky 17 (1999)[/b].[/h3]

USC: Counterforce and its prequel, Ultimate Space Commando, also take a lot of inspiration from some lesser-known games, a few [b]„hidden gems” from the late 1990s, the “age of 3D revolution”[/b]. While many developers were preoccupied with the evolving graphical capabilities of computers, and the addition of the third dimension, there were still titles that mainly focused on classic, almost [b]tabletop-like gameplay[/b], and still managed to bring something new and cool to the table.

One of these games is [b]Incubation: Time is Running Out (1997)[/b] by Blue Byte. It was a [b]turn- and tile-based, squad-oriented tactical game with a heavy focus on management of very limited actions per turn[/b]. It was heavily story-based, with a long campaign mode, and squad members you grew attached to and could equip with different gear, gadgets, and weapons, tailoring them to the tactics you wanted to use. During the whole game, you felt like your options were limited, but never your tactics: [b]this game really shined in shoehorning you into situations you could somehow still get out of alive if you found the proper tactics[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/ff97f63fe82d89da45827ad22d4d6f17f298d13d.jpg[/img]

There were some very unique mechanics that are not seen in many games: a well-implemented [b]weapon overheat system[/b] (instead of ammo); a [b]non-class- or skill-locked overwatch mode[/b] that[i]—since most enemies died from 1 or 2 shots—[/i]was very often important in stopping an alien before it reached you; a simple, but tactically [b]relevant use of elevations[/b]; and the[b] ability to control the battlefield with some items and weapons[/b][i]—for example, if you used the flamethrower, it created an area of impassable terrain for a few turns.[/i] Incubation also had a PvP game mode in which up to 4 players could fight against each other in asymmetric objective-based battles. [b]USC is directly inspired by the way Incubation handles overwatch (or “defense mode”) and the importance of facing in the right direction with your units[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/a721ec6b43f015331ba642cd8139f8dce7620371.jpg[/img]


Another game to mention is [b]Gorky 17 (also known as Odium, 1999)[/b] by Metropolis Software. It was also a very [b]heavily story-driven game[/b] in which a small group of NATO operatives had to fight to survive and to reveal the mystery behind the sudden appearance of hybrid creatures in a former Soviet military base in Poland.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/6db1eacd16814661625c641aff352de1d1380b5d.jpg[/img]

There was an “[b]exploration mode[/b]” where you moved around with your characters in real-time, discovering items, talking to people, and finding your way, but [b]whenever a combat situation ensued, the game would not only switch to turn-based but you and your enemies were put on a grid-based[/b], not-too-big battlefield, where the actual fighting took place. All weapons and items had their specific, very [b]board game-like mechanics[/b], and that, combined with the often [b]very confined spaces led to some rather interesting battle scenarios[/b]. Just like Space Crusade, Space Hulk, or Incubation, the [b]emphasis on smaller spaces and tighter rules was not a constraint[/b], but rather a playground for devising smart tactics. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/b9a26db9f1d8097d4985b73425a680374f555bea.png[/img]

In fact, I was so hooked on this approach to turn-based mechanics that I perfected dealing with the enemies using only the more basic weapons while stockpiling explosives and all kinds of nasty stuff for those really hard battles and[b] ended up completing the game with a whole nuclear arsenal still in my inventory[/b]... All said and done, I think Gorky 17 was not flawless, but still an excellent game, and showed yet another way, [b]another approach to how boardgame-like rules can be applied in a computer game, while making it feel like NOT a board game[/b].

Join our Discord to chat with us of USC Counterforce: https://discord.gg/vsxD6n8P8J

The USC Counterforce team

notes.title: Ready, set and fire for the Turn-based RPG Fest on Steam!
notes.content:
Hey marines,

We're honored to participate in the [b]Turn-Based RPG Fest on Steam[/b]! In USC: Counterforce, we’ve designed the turn-based mechanics to provide deep tactical options, delivering a challenging gameplay experience. As the player, you’ll control a squad of elite space marines, each with a certain amount of [b]Action Points[/b] that can be used in each turn. Whether it’s moving, attacking, deploying abilities, or interacting with the environment, every action matters. Effective positioning and smart use of cover are essential, as poorly placed units can quickly be eliminated.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/5a70d73532132efb398f62f68226167ea994c7c1.png[/img]

[h3]Immersive combat, unique strategy[/h3]

One of the major features of combat is the ability to[b] interact with the environment[/b]. Destructible objects and terrain give you the chance to turn the battlefield to your advantage—whether you’re blowing through walls or taking cover behind structures, the terrain can shape the flow of battle. Additionally, unit customization is a core part of our design. You can equip your marines with a variety of weapons and skills, creating devastating combos, such as freezing and shattering enemies or using acid and fire.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/daa50ebdb4eb04e01aff2335672616fb98223347.png[/img]
In Campaign mode, you’ll manage actions over planetary time phases, each representing three Earth hours. Balancing tasks like scanning, squad deployment, and engaging alien forces is crucial, as enemies evolve dynamically, pushing you to adjust your tactics quickly. During each Mission Time Phase, the Horde moves, seeking out any human presence. You'll receive resources based on the actions taken in the previous turn. The[b] time of day and weather also change[/b] on the planetary body.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/6d8f7399cbffcf778875a951b1e8fcdd2255226c.png[/img]
[h3]Be a leader to your squad[/h3]

The upgrade system plays a critical role in developing your squad’s capabilities. By collecting resources and materials, you can[b] upgrade weapons, gear, and equipment[/b], ensuring your marines are always prepared for tougher battles. Players can fine-tune their squads with upgrades tailored to their playstyle, creating a flexible progression system that rewards both aggressive and cautious strategies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/f368913f7288ab62a487adc8309441a368071028.png[/img]
Resource management is another vital component of our gameplay. Looting, when available, and ensuring your squad is stocked with enough ammunition is essential for survival. You can’t always rely on sheer firepower alone; planning when and where to gather resources will be critical to long-term success in the field.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/4b5e238df8bcf5427b5751a8e816aae13b149b97.png[/img]
Our AI and randomized encounters make sure each mission feels fresh, challenging, and unpredictable. Enemies react to your actions, and the Fog of War mechanic means that rushing headfirst into unknown territory can have devastating consequences, making cautious scouting a must.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/f0ae1eb9b1b7206822179abc632e2b6f08b73b45.gif[/img]

In summary, USC: Counterforce offers a [b]rich blend of tactical combat, environmental strategy, and resource management[/b]. Every decision you make has weight, and success will require both careful planning and adaptability. We’ve built this system to reward players who think ahead and adjust on the fly.

Enjoy the event and let's chat about your strategies and tactics in our Discord: https://discord.gg/vsxD6n8P8J

The USC Counterforce team

notes.title: Our retro inspirations
notes.content:
Hello Marines,

USC: Counterforce is inspired by a ton of retro references. Whether it's from 90's turn-based games or movies, you can easily understand that we have huge 80s and 90s inspirations.

This week is the perfect moment to deep dive into our inspirations as we are participating in Boomstock 2024, A celebration of all Boomer Shooters and kick-ass action games in general, all connected by their love for the good old days of gaming, shining through in the games’ artstyle, gameplay, or both!

For the following part, I [i]- Aliza, Lead Programmer -[/i] will take the mic. So let's dive into our references!

[h3]Aliens (1986) by James Cameron[/h3]

I will definitely start with [b]James Cameron's Aliens (1986)[/b], the sequel to Ridley Scott's sci-fi horror masterpiece Alien (1979).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/7d84ec6d176caee802182c6dbda96a049731bb9c.jpg[/img]
[i]Movie Poster of "Aliens" (1986) by James Cameron, www.plansamericains.com[/i]

[b]Aliens expands into the lore of what the Xenomorphs are as a species[/b], and pits a squad of hardened [b]marines[/b] against them, far away from any reinforcements or help. But, contrary to the original movie, it is shown the aliens, [i]though lethal[/i], and very terrifying in many ways, especially with their reproduction cycle, are indeed vulnerable, and these brave soldiers at least have some fighting chance. Humans also have what the Xenomorphs don't: technology, including nuclear warheads, and mechanized forklifts :) and airlocks, which ultimately lead to the demise of the hive and the alien queen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/954ceb207375299d4b6bdf977474c67f2b08007d.png[/img]
Left: [i]Screenshot in-game of the Reaper in USC: Counterforce[/i]
Right: [i]Image of the movie Aliens (1986) by James Caron, from the Dread Central website[/i]

[h3]I was about 12 when I saw the two movies, and ever since then, I was fascinated by the grim futuristic take on world-building and the mystery of the aliens.[/h3]

USC tries to summon the atmosphere--marines with state-of-the-art technology arrive to [b]clean up the planet after a mysterious incident with some "aliens"[/b], that turns out to be not really more than animals--[i]or maybe there's more about them?[/i] The task force is separated from any help and must fight for survival after things take a turn for the worst. Also, the in-game "head camera" is directly inspired by the body cameras in Aliens. In the Campaign, you'll also be able to launch tactical nukes on the planet's surface to eliminate nests, or hordes of aliens that are converging on your planetside positions. "That's the only way to be sure!"

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/77ac10c55942f168682646c23ff477dfd0c28ba9.png[/img]
[i]Screenshot of USC: Counterforce[/i]


For the good old games that greatly influenced USC: Counterforce. We always wanted to strike a [b]good balance between a kind of “realism” and old-school, boardgame-like combat mechanics[/b]—and though this is generally true about almost all games in the genre, we aim to [b]emphasize the game’s “tabletop feel”[/b] in many ways.

First of these is the completely [b]top-down presentation[/b] (at least as far as the tactical map screen goes, since you can also follow your marines through their head cameras)—and with this comes an almost completely flat map, without elevations and multi-story buildings. After Ultimate Space Commando we were experimenting with bringing elevations to its sequel, but ultimately, we found that it didn’t work well with the “flagship” USC mechanics, and it didn’t do good for the dynamic of the game. We didn’t want to change that special feeling that comes with this presentation, a feeling that made games like Julian Gollop’s [b]Laser Squad[/b] (1988-1992), [b]Space Hulk[/b] (board game: 1989, PC: 1993), or [b]Space Crusade[/b] (board game: 1990, Amiga/PC: 1992) so great.

We played these games as children back in the early 90s, and they made a huge footprint in our lives. [b]Equipping your squad with weapons, ammo, and armor to take on a mad scientist, defending your base, or fighting aliens in a jungle in Laser Squad was an experience second to none.[/b] You had Time Units to spend in each turn, carefully planning your movement and shots, consulting the scanner (minimap) to devise your tactics—and then being gunned down by a well-placed opportunity shot from the AI. You could destroy walls and obstacles, and it was important to be aware of your surroundings as you moved with your squad. Many choices with a comprehensible system behind them, forcing you to think, to make the best of each of your turns. If there was only one game to name as an influence for USC and USC: CF, it would be Laser Squad. We often tend to call squad- and turn-based games against aliens “UFO or X-Com-clones”, but really, those games only came after.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/0cc22ec09c2098e4463e3740654e0c382c5738ec.png[/img]
[i]Laser Squad "Screenshot 11" - Killed the enemy droid, mobygames.com [/i]

Space Hulk and Space Crusade, both parts of the Warhammer 40,000 universe, are a little bit different kinds of beasts, but only on the surface. You have a squad of hardened Space Marines; you have a grid-based map of tight corridors, rooms, and doors you can open. The rules are simpler, and your choices are not so abundant, but you have to [b]act almost perfectly in every situation to survive[/b]. Positioning of your units is key, as Line of Sight mechanics and other rules are very strict—these are board games, after all! And the atmosphere, the feeling of constant and imminent threat at every corner, while your Marines themselves are nothing short of a human war machine—[i]really unique![/i] When we look at the systems behind these games, we can see they differ a LOT from that of Laser Squad, but what they have in common makes them very fun, very engaging, and indeed very difficult games. Making something this engaging in 2022 is no small task—graphics and UX expectations may have evolved, but those in themselves don’t make a great tactical game! We can still learn a lot from games we played decades ago.

NEW

[*]Toggleable with a new information "(i)" button next to the minimap[/list]
[*]Added a special shortcut to the Campaign map (F7+F) that toggles the recently added free aim mode ON[list]

[*]Once you press F7+F, free aim mode is permanent in that playthrough from that point forward. It can't be switched back and forth.
[*]Note: if you (re)load a save that still doesn't have free aim mode enabled, you need to activate it again!
[*]The shortcut only works on the Campaign map, not during a mission.[/list]
[/list]

CHANGES

[list]
[*]Campaign: alien reinforcements in Horde eradication missions will arrive more consistently and in greater numbers, especially if the Horde is really large (150+)[list]
[*]Additional aliens will now start to arrive when 50% of the alien already in combat have been killed
[*]Reinforcements per wave: (remaining reinforcements / 3) + small default value (1-6, difficulty dependent); min. 11, max. 36[/list]
[*]Campaign: the number of alien reinforcements still incoming in Horde eradication missions is now displayed in the objective info
[*]Changed the icon for Armored Beta aliens to a different looking shield icon
[/list]

BALANCE/GAMEPLAY CHANGES

[list]
[*]"Seek & Destroy" missions (in Campaign: Horde eradication and some sub-missions in sites or spec. ops) no longer require that you kill ALL enemies:[list]
[*]The last alien, or the last few aliens if they are below "Reaper threat" overall, combined, won't count as mandatory targets
[*]The "Targets remaining" display will still reflect their total number, but you can expect the mission to end when it's 1, or just about 2-4 with confirmed smaller targets
[*]Nests won't count as mandatory targets at all
[*]Their number will still be shown in the objective info ("Nests: #") so you know, but this won't affect mission completion[/list]
[*]Campaign: aliens in Horde eradication will start to flee towards the map edges and leave the area (leading to a quickened victory) once their total number is greatly culled:[list]
[*]This works in tandem with the general update to S&D objective changes
[*]You can expect the aliens to withdraw once their sum total starting Action Points are less than 500 (about 10 larger units), so this depends on situation and difficulty level
[*]Aliens that were able to flee are considered defeated in global Campaign mechanics, so they won't linger around or return in some way in the sector[/list]
[*]Campaign: rate of amortization of structures & objects built in bases has been reduced to 15% per MP (down from 20%), and will stop at 40% of nominal value (was 5%)[list]
[*]Note: the same values for non-Campaign "Defend the Base!" games remain unchanged[/list]
[*]Campaign: mined raw Deothonit to crafting material conversion rate increased to 50:1 (from 100:1)
[*]Campaign: Asura-49 are now only worth 15 materials per piece (was 25)
[*]Deothonit fragments (loot from crystals in nests & mines) are now only worth 5 materials per piece (was 25)
[/list]

OPTIMIZATION

[list]
[*]Improved the way the game detects screen resolution:[list]
[*]If there are any issues during auto-detection and the display supports it, initial resolution will default to 1920x1080
[*]Resolutions with a "portrait" alignment (greater height than width) will not be falsely auto-detected, and will also not be an option in Settings
[*]Note: please check your screen resolution settings after the update![/list]
[*]Added a way to manually force a particular screen resolution:[list]
[*]0. Please start the game once just briefly after the update so it can create the new "display.ini" file
[*]1. Open the "display.ini" file in any text editor from "c:\Users\[your OS username]\AppData\LocalLow\Angry Cat Studios\USC Counterforce\"
[*]2. Change "forceResolution=0" under "[Resolution]" to "forceResolution=1"
[*]3. Change "width=1920", "height=1080", and "refresh=60" to the values you want
[*]4. Restart the game client
[*]If you experience any issues, you can just delete the file (it will be auto-created with default settings) or set forceResolution to 0, and start the game with auto-detect as before
[*]Note: when forcing a resolution, in-game resolution settings will still remain usable, but will revert to the forced resolution on every game client start[/list]
[*]Added a way to manually force a particular UI scaling (independent from resolution):[list]
[*]1. Open the "display.ini" file (see above)
[*]2. Change "forceCustomScaling=0" under "[UI]" to "forceCustomScaling=1"
[*]3. Change the value of "scalingFactor" to a value between 0.7 and 1.
[*]Note: setting "scalingFactor" to 1 will FORCE DISABLE UI scaling.[/list]
[/list]

FIXES

[list]
[*]Fixed a bug where the 15 extra bleeding from the Heavy arms primary specialization was sometimes applied to attacks with other weapons
[*]Campaign: fixed Resource Points to Deothonit conversion ratio inflation, preventing some exploits. Now there is a hard cap of max. 200 on selling and a min. 250 on buying.
[*]Campaign: fixed a regression introduced in the last hotfix that prevented managing a sector before you visited the Squad Assembly screen at least once (sorry!)

notes.content:
Hey marines,
 
A [b]new update[/b] is live now! And as the Summer has just begun, it is time to start your mission and the long-awaited [b]Campaign mode Beta[/b]! It's an [b]open Beta[/b], you can try this new mode and let us know your thoughts! The Steam Summer Sale is starting, and USC: Counterforce is [b]40% off until July 11[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/0a8cba7055e2d81bbe3c8f923db06c48c092133c.png[/img]

Explore what the Campaign mode has in store for you and experiment with its exclusive mechanics and features! You will be able to create your avatar, choose your affiliation, manage your marine roster, and go on the first missions of the Campaign, both on a global and small scale, with the strategic map!

Here are some important elements to know before you dive in:
[list]
[*] The translation in Simplified Chinese for the Campaign is still ongoing. This means that the Campaign Beta is currently only [b]partially localized in Simplified Chinese[/b] and will default to English for currently untranslated terms.
[*] The Campaign Beta previews its exclusive mechanics but [b]lacks final narrative content and objective progression[/b]. Expect potential issues, and [b]saved progress won’t carry over to v1.0[/b]. Full features will launch with the final update.
[/list]
[h3]Player Avatar Creation and Affiliation System[/h3]

Customize your Campaign and make impactful choices that influence your tactical opportunities while offering diverse pathways and outcomes, making each journey distinct and impactful.

[b]Avatar creation[/b]: In the new update adding the beta version of Campaign mode, you can now enjoy the feature of creating your own avatar and customizing it to reflect your unique style and preferences.
[b]Affiliation system[/b]: Additionally, you will be able to choose your affiliation. You can buy different upgrades, prototypes, and even nukes through each unique affiliation and make use of the black market for acquiring critical resources.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/da6af866fdac2b4100a7910cf909c334b0cda53a.jpg[/img]

[h3]Strategic Map and Persistent Mechanics[/h3]

The Campaign mode introduces the strategic map with global dynamic events but also small-scale sector-based missions. Your progression in the Campaign mode is persistent, this includes your inventory and marines.

[b]Sector-based missions[/b]: Each sector presents its own challenges, and you must strategically build and defend your bases against the ever-moving hordes of aliens! These missions will let you engage against alien hordes with a task force, explore derelict sites, and eradicate nests on-site.
[b]Strategic map layer[/b]: The map also features a dynamic weather and day-night system that affects outdoor missions, adapt your plan to the events of the map. Take direct control of any sector by landing squads and establishing an outpost, and also manage on a global scale by monitoring any activity on the planet, including alien hordes and weather events. Gather information and organize your course of action by scanning the sectors and nuking dangerous areas.
[b]Persistent progression[/b]: What you obtain, lose, and consume is persistent throughout the whole Campaign. This works for both units and inventory, which means that a [b]death is permanent[/b]. All your marines are unique and have their own XP bar and leveling systems, along with a status system tracking their availability, injuries, and condition, adding depth to the roster management and making each of your decisions critical for your long-term success or demise.
[b]New environment[/b]: Step into the crystal caves, available in nest missions!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/eb892b8b0e6e0c138afde506b9d12f9cd0a95bd9.png[/img]

[h3]Upcoming Features[/h3]

The Campaign mode Beta already brings a big part of what you will find in the full version on July 18. However, while the beta version showcases many new features, several key elements are still under development and will be available in the full release. These include the general campaign progression, the story and narrative with special missions and multiple outcomes, and your personalized avatar mechanics, including the game over and personal stake. Other content like corporation-given missions tied to the affiliation system, cutscenes, the Campaign tutorial, and the in-game help system are not yet implemented. It's also important to note that [b]save files from the Beta will not be compatible with the final release[/b]!

notes.title: Updated roadmap & Dev Diary #3—Campaign Squad Management Preview
notes.content:
Hey Marines!

Yesterday, we pushed the last major update before the 1.0 release. We know that some of you have questions regarding the Campaign. As a reminder, the [b]Campaign is still scheduled and will be added with the 1.0 version[/b]. On our side, we are still making good progress on it, and we really are excited to know your thoughts when it launches, and we think it's time to share our [b]new updated roadmap[/b] until the 1.0 release! As you can see, we plan to [b]release the game in July 2024[/b], so be ready for the Campaign coming soon!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/81fb33b401787d30377e6a8d1882f71f0c288701.png[/img]

Now, back to today Dev Diary about the [b]general mechanics[/b] of the [b]squad management[/b]!

[h3]General Campaign mechanics[/h3]

[h3]Squad management[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/f2ee9c944a8e37b6e4cee95bbcf5b8f76c1d0514.png[/img]

The Squad Assembly screen you know from the preparation phase of a mission in the other game modes will be familiar, but with many, many changes that befit the new and changed mechanics of the Campaign.

One of the most important differences is that you have a fixed starting roster of 30 marines, including [b]your avatar[/b], the returning crew of U.S.C. Wraith (15 marines), and 14 (randomized) marines from your fleet. All of them have preset skills and ranks, with some spare skill points left, so you can start training them in the direction you want to from the get-go. Unlike non-Campaign games, units will gain [b]Experience Points[/b] (XP) for all kinds of actions they perform and, with that, achieve promotions that give them new skill points and other perks. “Demoting” or re-organizing their skills will not be an option, nor will resurrecting the dead (yes, we are talking about [b]permadeath[/b]!). Sometimes you’ll have to wait until you can re-deploy a marine (if they are seriously injured or assigned to a somewhat longer task or mission, etc.), so you’ll have to make sure you don’t only have an “A-Team” of 6 killing machines but more reliable individuals to send on missions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/d4a8aac6ebfb94db57d1a7f17dae58b05fd8a8c6.png[/img]

The other big difference is how [b]global inventory[/b] is handled. In the Campaign, all items are [b]“status persistent”[/b], which in this case actually means that if they’re gone, they’re gone. There are no “loadout configurations” that are reset after a mission, as every bullet you fire or medikit you use is spent forever; your inventory can change swiftly, and you have to work with what you have, not with what you’d think is optimal. You will, however, start with a great assortment of weapons, ammo, and equipment, as well as a good pool of crafting materials; you’ll feel powerful and unstoppable… until you realize that reinforcements are weeks away and your supplies deplete quickly. The time will come to clear the dust from those good old, reliable .44 pistols! Of course, you will be able to craft anything if you have the resources. And don’t forget, “status persistence” for items also means that what you pick up and bring home is truly yours to keep (or to disassemble for materials…)!

With that, “squad configurations” are also gone. For each mission, you can decide freely who to deploy. You can configure up to 3 squads of 6–6 marines in many cases. Having good intel will help you decide how many marines to bring and what equipment they should carry for a specific mission.

[h3]Missed our previous dev diaries on the Campaign? You can read them here:[/h3]
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1574870/view/3883854408804767159
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1574870/view/4211502692132648548

Stand by for more information about the Campaign and upcoming sneak peeks!

The USC: Counterforce team

[/list][/list]

[list]

[/list][/list]
[list]
[*] New item: Force field emitter[list]
[*] Creates an impassable, indestructible energy barrier on a grid for a max. of 5 turns

[*] Can be easily toggled on/off, or disarmed and picked up for reusing later
[/list][/list]

[*] New single mission map type: Desolate canyon[list]

notes.title: Dev Diary #2—Campaign Mechanics Preview
notes.content:
Hey Marines!

The [b]Campaign[/b] is progressing nicely, and we're still burning the midnight oil on it. As we explained in our previous Dev Diary, it includes a [b]grand strategic layer[/b] on a [b]planet map[/b]. And it's high time to talk about the planet map and how it works. Let's dig into the [b]general mechanics[/b] and strategic map layer in today's dev diary!

[h3]General Campaign mechanics[/h3]

The [b]Campaign progress[/b] in USC: Counterforce will be completely [b]separate from[/b] the other [b]game modes[/b]. This means you don’t need to unlock items or gather resources before you can attempt a playthrough, as all content will be available to you from the start—though some items or options will be tied to other Campaign-specific conditions. The Campaign will feature a partly [b]narrative-driven[/b], [b]open-ended story[/b] that plays out on a planetwide strategic map, allowing for a great deal of tactical and diplomatic choices along the way, as well as for managing your inventory and units on a persistent basis. Your marines will gain XP and ranks, your items and ammo will deplete and need to be restocked by looting during missions and crafting, and the dead will stay dead (but, of course, you’ll be able to reload a previous save unless you play on “Hardcore”).

[h3]The strategic layer[/h3]

There will be a lot happening on the strategic map. Time in the Campaign is divided into [b]Mission Time Phases[/b] (MP for short), each taking up 3 Earth hours, adding up to a total of 15 hours per day on M-8322, consisting of 5 distinct daylight phases. An MP is like a Turn during a mission, but on a global scale: when you’ve performed every action you wanted, you pass it, and the next MP begins—and between the two, of course, the aliens and the environment also get their “turns.” Alien hordes will move, join together, or disappear into subterranean caves, nests will grow, evolve, and expand to neighboring sectors; sandstorms and electromagnetic storms will pass through the desolate wastes of the planet.
In your turn, you can scan the surface to discover ruins and nests, or pinpoint the movement of hordes. You can utilize your nuclear arsenal from orbit to obliterate the surface of any sector—but be warned! Not only do you have a limited supply of nuclear warheads, but bombing left and right has other, long-term consequences, both trivial and latent.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/0f147d5e75fafe5203bb26dcd70c9ef0ed71b4f1.png[/img]

You can also take direct control of any sector by landing squads and [b]establishing an outpost[/b]. You can use these to set up defenses in anticipation of a horde passing through, or, what is even more important, to start mining Deothonit, the single most valuable material in the known universe (also the most valuable crafting material in the game, that can be converted into anything except Asura-49, which comes from alien specimens). [b]Base building mechanics[/b] are based on the [i]Defend the Base![/i] game mode, but instead of having to defend a base wave after wave, you can pop in and out to manage it, and an actual “defense phase” will only take place when it is attacked. Building bases and mining is a good way to gather crafting materials, but it’s not mandatory. There are other ways to get enough supplies if base management is not your cup of tea, or you just prefer another approach in a playthrough.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/6d8f7399cbffcf778875a951b1e8fcdd2255226c.png[/img]

Sending squads to the location of known nests or hordes to attack them directly is also an option. Nest-busting missions are [b]multi-phase operations[/b] where you have to infiltrate an underground cave system. From time to time, other mission options will also pop up: you can be contacted by USCF Command or one of the mega-concerns to help their bases or perform some other assignment on their behalf. These are good opportunities to gain their favor and special support—but never mandatory to do if you have other plans!

The progress of your campaign is measured by [b]3 global gauges[/b]: Intelligence, Control, and Threat. None of them are “victory/defeat conditions” on their own, but they play a great role in shaping your story. A high [b]Intelligence[/b] means you know a lot about the planet, enemy behavior, and other important topics; this can open up additional avenues to what you think victory means for you. Similarly, [b]Control[/b] measures your effective power over the planet: the sectors you actually control, have cleansed, or rebuilt. The [b]Threat gauge[/b] is also complex: of course, it will go down if you continually eradicate aliens, but they also have their agenda and “victory conditions”, and some other actions you take—or fail to take in time—will advance it. But whatever happens, the Campaign is not about filling a gauge. These are just data that help you comprehend the situation. The fate of the planet (and maybe Humankind) is always determined by actual, tactical gameplay scenarios.

[h3]Missed our previous dev diary on the Campaign? You can read it here:[/h3]
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1574870/view/3883854408804767159

Stay tuned for more extra details about the Campaign. We're not done giving you sneak peaks into what we've been focusing on and what awaits you!

The USC: Counterforce team

notes.title: Wrath of Zeus major update!
notes.content:
Hey Marines,

A new [b]major update[/b] is live now! Spring approaches and the sun shines a little longer to fill your marines with hope as we bring a fair share of new gear and mechanics to fight back the alien threat! Enjoy the [b]Steam Spring Sale[/b], the game is discounted ([b]40% off[/b]) from today to March 21!

Special delivery for your marines (signed with your feedback)! This major update brings two new weapons, a new mechanic, UI improvements, and more unlockable items with the Gear Tokens.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/bb3e352432b5d74a3b71da023cd8f27ec2707adb.jpg[/img]

[h2]New weapon & new shield[/h2]

We organized a vote on Discord and Twitter to let you choose the next weapon you’ll experiment with, and you chose the [b]Energy Rifle[/b]! The arsenal of the USC commandos has received yet another significant upgrade with this weapon and a [b]new shield[/b]!
[list]
[*] [b]Energy Rifle[/b]: A marvel of high-tech engineering designed to give your marines the upper hand on the battlefield. This expensive and "electrifying" small arm, available without unlocking, is a powerful weapon. It deals a lot of damage and can set aliens on fire. This weapon comes with two attack modes:
[list]
[*] "[b]Controlled impulse[/b]", a single-target attack in a star pattern with a low AP cost and significant damage potential.
[*] "[b]Discharge[/b]", a 3x3 area with a free pattern attack, capable of inflicting substantial damage.
[/list][*] [i]This weapon doesn't deal electric damage (because this damage type doesn't exist in the game), but rather Tranquilization and Fire damage! So fear not, you can fire at will even in flooded areas of the Hydroponics environment![/i]

[*] [b]Energy Shield[/b]: A more expensive alternative to the Riot shield, with added benefits: better protection from Shadow damage and better defensive values.
[/list]
This Energy Rifle relies on [b]Energy Charge ammunition[/b]. With these two new additions to your gear, you'll be prepared to exterminate even the toughest of aliens!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/daa50ebdb4eb04e01aff2335672616fb98223347.png[/img]
[i]See? No problem zapping aliens around in the flooded areas![/i]


[h2]Community-based features and balance[/h2]

Thanks to your suggestions, we designed and added a [b]new mechanic[/b] using a set of small arms with a shield. This mechanic is called "[b]Close Quarters Weapon[/b]" ([b]CQW[/b]).
[list]
[*] It allows your marines to wield a [b]small arm while holding a shield[/b]. They will now benefit from [b]defensive bonuses[/b] even when not in melee attack mode.
[*] The CQW weapons are the following: Self-Defense Pistol, Bulleteer, Shotgun, and QuadSeeker. All the weapons that are classified as CQW have a "pistol" icon (they are still considered "small arm" weapons).
[/list]Make the most of this new mechanic to adapt your strategy and operate differently on the battlefield!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/4b5e238df8bcf5427b5751a8e816aae13b149b97.png[/img]

To continue expanding the possibility of unlocking gear with [b]Gear Tokens[/b], you can now also obtain [b]crafting recipes[/b] but at a considerable cost, since these are end-game progression items for non-Campaign modes.
[i]As a reminder, Gear Tokens can be obtained by completing a game in any non-Campaign mode, and the amount received depends on the difficulty level. You can still acquire items by completing the corresponding challenges while also obtaining Gear Tokens[/i].

The [b][i]Defend the Base![/i][/b] mode has been reworked and balanced, with aliens now being [b]more aggressive[/b] towards structures, creating shortcuts, and destroying crucial objects to hinder your objectives. The initial design of the first AI wave has been reintroduced with balance tweaks, with aliens [b]attacking[/b] again during the [b]AI first turn[/b]. AI can skip turns on arrival, reducing movement AP costs by 1 for one turn. [b]More aliens[/b] will arrive during the first turn of each wave, and turrets are slightly more expensive. Structure and object value amortization rates per wave have been increased, making it more important to plan your initial base accordingly, as relocating is now more costly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/2753f360e403e28910e48314731a01996755308d.png[/img]

[h2]UI improvements[/h2]

The UI has also undergone improvements, and we designed a new in-mission feature:
[list]
[*] The [b]Squad Overview Panel[/b]. It provides a comprehensive view of all active (alive) units across multiple squads, allowing for better coordination and resource management during missions.
[*] The panel is also available during the Construction phase in Defend the Base! mode, providing the much needed information to make better decisions about what supplies to order, etc.
[*] We have also added the possibility to change to [b]hotkeys[/b] for the [b]UI and information display[/b] of this new panel and other tactical view markers and outlines in the Settings > Interface and Settings > Misc. menus, respectively. Customize and adapt the interface to suit your playstyle!
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/9e7dda1dee930de7199a30282be22a07e7e9f834.png[/img]

Read the full patch notes [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1574870/view/4148449764369304233][b]here[/b][/url].

https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1574870/view/4148449764369304233

All clear for now! Keep your eyes peeled for further updates on USC: Counterforce and the challenges that lie ahead!

notes.title: The Weapon Prototype system
notes.content:
Hey Marines!

Time to do some math! We’re going to break down the [b]weapon prototype system[/b]. You can improve your gear with prototypes. When you successfully complete a Single Mission within the given bonus deadline, you receive 1 or 2 randomized Prototype Weapons. These are enhanced versions of a weapon already available to you in Squad Assembly, with some additional and/or modified properties.

The number of Prototypes you get depends on the mission [b]Difficulty[/b] AND your [b]Performance Score[/b]. To know your exact chance of getting a second Prototype (one is guaranteed under the conditions stated above), multiply the Difficulty level (0–6; 0 for Beginner, 6 for Ultimate) with your Performance Score (0–100). If this value is less than 250, you will only get 1 Prototype. If the value is between 250 and 449, you have a chance for a second one, proportional to how close you are to 449. If the value is 450 or above, you are guaranteed to get 2 Prototypes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/cd8a60b68e8fdea176dbd9cba38d571143499bf0.png[/img]

Each Prototype you get is first assigned a [b]Mark (I–IX)[/b] and an [b]overall Quality Level (1–100[/b]). The Mark of a Prototype determines what kind of properties it can potentially have. The Quality Level determines the quality range of each of its properties and also factors into how many properties the weapon will ultimately have.

Mark is a random value between Difficulty + 1 and Difficulty + 3. On Beginner, you can only get a Prototype up to Mark III. On Ultimate, you will get a Mark VI in the worst case.

[h3]Quality (Q) is calculated by the following formula:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Q = 15 + Difficulty × (Performance Score / 10) + [a random integer between -25 and (Performance Score / 2)], clamped between 1 and 100
[/list]

The number of enhancements (properties) is a random value between (Mark / 3) × (Q / 100f) and (Mark / 2) × (Q / 100f), plus 1. The maximum number of properties is 5. (The “f” after 100 here denotes that we’re keeping the fragments in the result for that operation; otherwise, we’re always flooring the results.)

Then, for each enhancement the weapon will have, its exact type and individual quality are determined. This individual quality (q) is a random value between Q / 2 and Q (the weapon’s Quality Level).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/94a02462b8da5445e41b2bde1777cc9daca32489.png[/img]

Below you find a table of all the possible enhancements (properties). In this table, Mark refers to the minimum Mark a weapon must have for the chance to get the corresponding enhancement. Min. and Max. show the minimum and maximum values between which the enhancement’s effect will get its actual strength, based on its quality (q = 1: minimum; q = 100: maximum; 1 < q < 100: linearly proportional value). Values are generally added to the weapon’s respective property value.

The crafting cost of a Prototype depends both on its Mark and its overall Quality Level. The common four materials are always required, but Portable batteries are only needed for Mark IV and above, Electrical components for Mark V and above, Asura-49 for Mark VI and above, and Deothonit for Mark VII and above only.

[i]Note: Don't worry! The game will handle the math behind the prototype system. Your task is to acquire these prototype weapons and eliminate the enemy.[/i]

[b]Example:[/b]

You complete a mission on Intense difficulty (3) and gets a Performance Score of 80. 3 × 80 = 240, which is less than 250, so they will only get a single Prototype. They have the chance for a Prototype between Mark IV and Mark VI – let’s say they get a Mark V. The Quality Level (Q) is 15 + 3 × (80 / 10) + [a random integer between -25 and (80 / 2)]. Let’s say this random roll is 11; so, Q is 15 + 24 + 11 = 50. Oh, and they get an Assault rifle—this was also determined randomly.

The next part, to get the number of enhancements is a bit trickier. We’re going to floor the results of the Mark divisions, but use fragments for the Quality divisions (that’s what the “f” after 100 denotes): random between (5 / 3) × (50 / 100f) and (5 / 2) × (50 / 100f), plus 1 thus becomes random between 1 × 0.5 and 2 × 0.5, plus 1. So, the random part is between (we’re flooring again for the final result) 0 and 1 – and we’re then also adding 1. Thus, if we’re lucky (50% chance in this instance), this Prototype can have 2 properties. Let’s say we are!

It’s a Mark V, so we can get any of the properties up to Impact force. Let’s say we get that, and Ammo capacity for the second one. For each property we get a random quality (q) between 25 and 50: say we got 33 and 40. The range for Impact force is between 10 and 20; q = 33 means it will have a final value of 13. Ammo capacity is between 1.1 and 2.0; with q = 40, it will be ((2.0 – 1.1) / 100f) × 40 + 1.1 = 0.009 × 40 + 1.1 = 0.36 + 1.1 = 1.46. (We calculated the value that is 40% “halfway” between 1.1 and 2.) The default ammo capacity of the Assault rifle is 40, so this will have a capacity of 40 * 1.46 = 58.4, floored to 58. And each attack with it will have +13 Armor Penetration compared to whatever it would otherwise be.

[h3][b]Summary[/b]: The higher the completed mission's difficulty results in a higher Mark rank Prototype blueprint that can be crafted of the looted materials. Using these weapons means extra abilities are applied during combat! So, you can assemble a more effective Squad, and thus, you can complete higher difficulty levels.[/h3]

Now you're all set! Stay tuned for more updates on the game development. We're not done sharing sneak peeks at what we're working on and what's waiting for you!

We read all your comments and feedback, so feel free to [b]share your thoughts[/b] and help us in making USC: Counterforce the best game possible!

[i]There's no more time to waste, Commander! A lot of bugs are waiting for you. Dismissed.[/i]

The USC: Counterforce team

notes.title: Hydroponic Hell major update!
notes.content:
Hey Marines!

Happy New Year, marines! A [b]new major update[/b] is [b]live now[/b]—forget your new year resolutions and just appreciate that your marines get to live to see another day!

Our new major update brings an [b]end[/b] to the [b]limited-time Xmas event[/b]. Time to discover your rewards! Explore the murky waters of the [b]new environment[/b]: Hydroponics, and face a [b]new insect-like flying alien[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/3cd4e3d1afd0c5906b7ae681adf016cb41129cce.png[/img]

[b]Acidya[/b]: An insect-like flyer and quite a nasty bug.
[list]
[*] Its [b]flying abilities[/b] allow it to avoid ground hazards.

[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/77ac10c55942f168682646c23ff477dfd0c28ba9.png[/img]

[b]Hydroponics[/b]: This new environment adds its share of changes in terms of gameplay with an [b]environmental modifier[/b]! Single Mission mode now has [b]two new map types[/b]: Hydroponic Labs and Hydro-engineering level. A [b]new Operation[/b] is now available in the Hydroponics environment too.
[list]
[*] [b]Flooding[/b] (in Hydro-engineering level map type and in specific missions in the new Operation for now): Water reaches you at waist-height. Your movements and aliens’ are hindered, costing more APs. Because the area is flooded, fire doesn’t affect you in this watery environment.
[*] Good news is, you won’t find Scorpions, Skitters, Swarmers, or Leeches there! Bad news is, your Flamethrower and Bio-rifle are not a good fit in such a place, since dispersion won’t work there.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/3684892a0fd66c32aea38ad1ff0a4b1d062a5b9c.png[/img]

[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/0694289fc1f5e36d0fa37ac58403f36ec2cc3b46.png[/img]

[h2]Community suggestions[/h2]

Your [b]feedback[/b] allowed us to add a [b]new way of unlocking gear[/b] without completing missions in higher difficulties by gathering [b]Gear Tokens[/b] and spending them on the Squad Assembly screen. Gear Tokens can be obtained by completing a game in any non-Campaign mode, and the amount received depends on the difficulty level. You can still acquire items by completing the corresponding challenges (and while also obtaining Gear Tokens).

Read the full patch notes [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1574870/view/3953665275847242815]here[/url][/b].

Over and out! Stay on the lookout for more updates on USC: Counterforce and challenges to face!

❄️ The USC: Counterforce team

notes.title: Dev Diary #1—Campaign Feature Preview
notes.content:
Hey Marines!

The [b]Campaign[/b] in USC:CF will feature a [b]grand strategic layer[/b] on a planet map, [b]persistent global inventory management[/b], [b]unit progression with XP gains[/b] and [b]permadeath[/b], narrative elements with lore & choices, and even more, compared to the non-Campaign game modes. But how will the Campaign start, what choices will the player have in creating a Campaign session, and how will those affect the course of the game? Today, we’re going to tell you a bit more about this.

[h3]Starting a Campaign[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/79de06e8f04d836f68aac17e0dc1a269a23a99c2.png[/img]
From the Main Menu you’ll find yourself on the Campaign setup screen. The Campaign will feature a [b]slot-based save system[/b], but that doesn’t mean you can’t save manually or [b]have multiple saves if you’re not playing on Hardcore[/b] (“Iron Man")—the main purpose of this system is to let you easily differentiate between save files belonging to different playthroughs!

In addition to the [b]Difficulty setting[/b] known from the other game modes, which will not only control enemy number and strength but also the amount of loot and some other elements (don’t forget, in the Campaign, what items and ammo you spend will remain spent—you'll have to find means to replenish the stock!), there’s the Campaign length/complexity setting that controls how big a war you’re getting yourself into. With the [b]Story option[/b], the background simulation that runs the alien hordes and controls the flow of the whole Campaign will be more simplistic, letting you follow a clear path and finish the story in 15-20 hours if everything goes well. On [b]Normal[/b], you’ll see much more alien activity and more battles, will have to make more strategic choices, and will have to be wiser with your spending and overall management to be able to complete the story in about 50 hours. Full-scale is for the real strategy enthusiast who is not afraid to micro-manage everything—many, many battles await against an enemy on multiple fronts, against the scarcity of resources, and the weight of all choices that cannot be unmade.

[h3]Affiliation[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/70fbefb5faac60b4342b1142a12aae5c1b9533d9.png[/img]
As a Fleet Commander of the USCF, you’re not above the intricacies of global politics and corporate espionage. The greatest mega-concerns that run Earth in 2308 have a huge stake in all United Space Command activity, and not everyone is always playing by the book—of course not! At the beginning of the game, you’ll have to [b]choose an affiliation[/b]—[b]or you can choose not to have one outside of USC[/b]. This choice will [b]affect your Relations and Renown[/b], two new systems that will be important during the Campaign. By navigating the world of politics, agreeing to or rejecting (or failing!) secret missions, selling information to, or withholding intelligence from the different firms, your Relations with them will change. A good relationship will grant you perks, like access to exclusive weapons and items. Renown, on the other hand, measures your dignity as an officer, and if you don’t engage in fishy agreements with non-military agencies, that will boost it dearly. [b]Renown may be used in a far subtler way than Relations[/b], like facilitating a resolution between warring factions, requesting additional reinforcements, or holding the morale of your crew high even when things go awry. [b]The Relations and Renown system will be a secondary layer to the Campaign[/b], one you can mostly ignore if you’re only interested in the war strategy, but it will give your choices even more weight in certain situations. And of course, every mega-concern may have a hidden agenda that can influence the course of the war, so you’d better be prepared!

[h3]Personal avatar[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/d00c0e5e319ebaf83155c0bcb0183b6ef0e06e96.png[/img]
You didn’t think you could wage war remotely on a planet many lightyears away from Earth, did you? You, as Commander, will be among your marines aboard the deck of your flagship and will have the option to go into battle with them when you want, or when the necessity arises. At the start of the Campaign, you will be asked to [b]customize your avatar[/b]. [b]This avatar will be one of the many units on the roster[/b], representing you, personally. You can choose not to go into battle yourself, and if everything goes well, you’ll never have to; but fighting alongside your marines can boost their morale and your Renown. Some secret missions from affiliations will also require that you oversee the operation in person. And, of course, if the flagship—horribile dictu!—ever gets attacked, you’ll have to fight for your life alongside your fellow crewmates. [b]If your avatar dies, the game is immediately over[/b]—but, of course, you [b]can always reload a previously saved game[/b]… granted you’re not playing on Hardcore!

[b]Stay tuned for more updates on the Campaign[/b]. We're not done sharing sneak peeks at what we're working on and what's waiting for you!

❄️ The USC: Counterforce team 🎁

notes.title: Halloween update and new enemies!
notes.content:
Hey Marines!

A [b]new major update is live now[/b] and your commandos’ nightmare has just begun! [b]New aliens[/b] are joining the horde and are going to make them wish they never stepped foot on this cursed planet M8322.

This major update to celebrate Halloween comes with a [b]new weapon[/b], the [b]flamethrower[/b], and new enemies: [b]Reaper Mother[/b], her [b]Leech eggs[/b] and hatchling [b]Leeches[/b], [b]Organ Shepherd[/b] and [b]Greater Shadow Envoy[/b]. This new content will be [b]added permanently[/b] to the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/b60eeaa747ac6d1a474a31db1a5a078153dbddf6.gif[/img]

[h2]New aliens[/h2]

[list]
[*][b]Reaper Mother[/b]: This entity surpasses its Reaper kin. Its size and its strength set it apart along with its ability to lay Leech eggs once per turn. This ability forces you to redirect your focus on it if you do not want to be overwhelmed, adding a new layer of complexity to the fight.
[list]
	[*][b]Leech egg[/b]: They do not appear on the battlefield by default. They are laid only once per turn, when a Reaper Mother engages the player. Provoking a Leech egg requires inflicting damage on it, as proximity alone won't trigger its emergence. You must proceed carefully, as these eggs will inevitably hatch on the third turn after being laid, unleashing high HP Leeches, but with little to no armor.
	[*][b]Leech[/b]: These feisty creatures are not on the map, but appear from eggs. They exhibit traits similar to Skitters, but distinguish themselves with exceptionally high life-stealing capabilities. Their attacks deliver a double whammy of paralysis (tranquilization) and extra bleeding, making them dangerous foes that demand precision and resourcefulness to defeat. This new breed of enemy intensifies the encounter with their Reaper Mother.
[/list]
[*][b]Organ Shepherd[/b]: This gruesome fleshy monster is the aliens' attempt to mimic humanoid physiology. Agile and capable of paralyzing and bleeding attacks, this creature's tactics vary depending on the situation. It may target a single victim when in melee range or strike a group of targets within the proximity of two grids. In addition to its deadly melee capabilities, it wields a spit attack similar to the Alpha Wormpig's, afflicting paralysis and bleeding effects. The Organ Shepherd stands as a tough adversary, being completely impervious to tranquilization, forcing you to adapt and find alternative ways to deal with it.
[*] [b]Greater Shadow Envoy[/b]: This terrifying foe meets all the criteria of an apex predator. It outshines all previous enemies you have met so far in terms of power. Its area-of-effect melee attack is so potent that it can ignite Shadow fires on the grids it impacts, further complicating your survival plan and escape. With high fire resistance, this menace will make you despair and hope for a quick death.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/f768eb7bcba6a1aea427d0012e699b20b2a84e97.png[/img]

[h2]New weapon and hydrazine mechanics[/h2]
[list]
[*] The challenges posed by these new threats call for new ways to exploit the battleground. Hydrazine is also available in squad management and found during missions. [b]It can now be spilled on adjacent grids[/b] that do not have ground effects like radiation pools or fire. [b]Even on an enemy grid[/b] if the situation permits! Spilling Hydrazine consumes both 1 ammo stack and 8 Action Points (the cost scales with Field Expertise skills). [b]Spilled Hydrazine pool causes explosions if lit on fire[/b]. It deals damage ranging from 50 to 100, with an additional 200 fire damage and Armor Penetration of 20. This explosion also has a 50% chance of affecting adjacent targets, creating opportunities for you to turn the tide in their favor.
[*] To combat these new threats, [b]you can now wield[/b] the infamous [b]flamethrower[/b]! [b]This heavy weapon utilizes Hydrazine[/b] as ammunition. This weapon offers two powerful attack modes. The first, "[b]Line Ignite[/b]", enables you to unleash flames in a line spanning five grids, making it a critical choice when dealing with multiple targets. However, it's essential to note that [b]this attack mode doesn't work in areas with no atmosphere[/b] (in the case of hull breaches). The second attack mode, "[b]Disperse[/b]", allows you to spray Hydrazine on the ground, creating a 3x3 area of upcoming fiery chaos. Due to the inherent nature of these attacks, [b]neither can be utilized in Defense Mode[/b], you must use this weapon carefully.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/bafc8aba8c3f2b1f442a8a82e3a531601535f3bb.gif[/img]

Read the full patch notes [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1574870/view/3732978109561936942]here[/url].

Equip your flamethrower and study these new foes. [b]Stay tuned for more information on the upcoming content during Early Access![/b]

notes.title: Map creation: randomization process
notes.content:
Hey Marines!

As you’ve been exploring the planetary body M-8322, you have noticed that [b]the map changes with every deployment[/b]. USC: Counterforce features [b]procedurally generated maps and missions[/b]. But what does this mean? What can you expect when playing the different game modes? In this article, we’re going to answer these questions, and also take a look at more nuanced technicalities for the acute soldiers who enjoy knowing how this all works.

First off, [b][i]every single mission[/i] you play in the game is procedurally generated[/b]—at least the map you’re playing on. We use our [b]homemade random map generator (RMG) algorithm[/b] tailored to fit the exact needs of the game to do this. But random doesn’t mean "uncontrolled". [b]Specific map and mission parameters[/b] are fed to the RMG [b]as invariables[/b], as rules that need to be satisfied under all conditions. But whatever is not "fixed", will be randomized. So, for example, a Single Mission with the objective "Reach extraction point" will always have insertion and extraction zones far away from each other, but otherwise, the layout of the actual map will be random, including which corner of the map those zones are in. In missions during the various Operations, more rules are enforced: we can tell the RMG to "seal off" complete areas of the map by making impassable walls and narrow connections, or we can control where buildings should be on the surface, etc.

But there’s more to it than the layout of the map. [b]Objects, items, and even aliens are placed randomly.[/b] Of course, the placement algorithms for these elements also follow rules. The [b]total number of aliens[/b] (per species) [b]is controlled by the difficulty level and other parameters[/b], but the [b]exact composition of the horde[/b] (Alphas, Betas) [b]is randomized[/b], as are their starting locations on the map. The items you can find in crates during a mission are also random, but we use "loot tables" for different room types to determine what kind of equipment you can find in a crate you open there.

Now let’s see how this works a little bit closer, so you can get an idea of the depth of randomness and control we can use already, and in the future in new game modes. The map generator works in multiple passes, and we can exert constraints or randomization separately in all of these.

[h3]Pass 1: Layout descriptor[/h3]

This is a lot of data that describes various [b]properties of the mission and the map[/b], including objectives, environment, etc. At this point, we can already use randomization for almost all parameters (size, time of day, number of nests, position of starting zone, etc.), or specify the ones we want, selectively. This means we can use the system either to make a very specific mission or a completely random mission with a few selected fixed properties.

[h3]Pass 2: Layout generator (RLG)[/h3]

Based on the rules and settings in a layout descriptor, the RLG creates a [i]logical map layout[/i] that adheres to all specified rules, and other invariants (like all parts of the map should be accessible via a door, etc.). Mind you, this is not yet a map! [b]It contains data about [i]nodes[/i] that have connections with each other[/b], join into bigger rooms, or are excluded from the effective map area. At this point, we can check and ensure the general properties of a map without dealing with, say, 1024 or more grids directly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/61d296b8516643582989d0c67df25f04dc95a143.png[/img]

[h3]Pass 3: "Inflation"[/h3]

The [b]layout is converted into an actual map[/b] made of grids based on specific map parameters. At this point, we can use the very same layout to create a map with small rooms and narrow corridors, or one with bigger rooms and wider corridors, while [i]logically[/i] it is still very similar to the first one. In the picture below, you can see the same layout resulting in different maps due to a different "room size" inflation setting:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/6cf870358aac18b2c6876c0693cace5f111cb27d.png[/img]

Or we can instruct the generator to make all walls single-width, which not only results in another kind of layout, but also greatly differs gameplay-wise (aliens can break through much sooner, etc.). In the picture below, you see a map with this sort of layout. You can also see that the extraction zone is placed in the opposite corner from the insertion point—all other elements are randomized.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/ab701de48072f209117bb3c408389c76c3e643db.png[/img]

[b]Connections[/b] are also [b]converted into doors that have many randomizable properties[/b] (single or double, locked, hardwired, etc.). Specific environments (for example, mines and caves) have other special rules that modify how the actual "rooms" are processed—for example, protruding wall segments can be placed in addition. In the picture below, you can see some of these extra features.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/05c559548738fc58d8bb268c1b6fa53960fd2fce.png[/img]

[h3]Pass 4: Population[/h3]

This process has many sub-passes to ensure everything is put where it needs to be. Floor hazards, static and usable objects, generators, nests, service tunnel hatches, and finally, aliens and marines. Placement rules for each type of thing can be overridden or extended (for example, a few extra item crates with specific items are placed in a specific region of the map, etc.).

Balance in a game like USC: Counterforce is one of the most important things, and one crucial factor in creating it is the very map you play on. We think [b]randomness brings a lot of uncertainty, tension, and replayability to the game[/b], but it’s also important to "control the chaos" to some extent. [b]We’re constantly iterating on these aspects of the game during development[/b] and [b]continuously adding new elements[/b], so you can expect even more interesting scenarios and death traps!

Now that you know the behind-the-scenes details of the maps you've been exploring, this will help you come up with new tactics to assess the battlefield!

The USC: Counterforce

notes.title: Five tips to start USC: Counterforce
notes.content:
USC: Counterforce is in [b]Early Access now on Steam[/b]. It's [b]time to prepare yourself[/b] to fight off the alien hordes in this thrilling top-down squad tactics revival.

To set you up for success and ensure you keep your focus on what matters most, we've compiled five essential tips. These insights will guide your mindset, highlighting key priorities and crucial elements to watch out for in the game.

Before you board that spaceship to take out the alien threat, there are a few things you should know, whether this is your first time on the planetary body M-8322 or not. A well-advised marine is better than a dead one. Get ready to immerse yourself in strategic gameplay and embark on an exciting adventure in USC: Counterforce!

[b]Here are some tips to improve your chances of surviving and succeeding:[/b]

[h3]Summary[/h3]
[b]Tip #1[/b] Balance and Adapt Your Squad
[b]Tip #2[/b] Analyze the Environment
[b]Tip #3[/b] Loot, Upgrade, Craft
[b]Tip #4[/b] Combos & Buildups
[b]Tip #5[/b] Encyclopedia/Wiki


[h1]#1 Balance and Adapt Your Squad[/h1]

USC: Counterforce places a strong emphasis on teamwork and coordination.
When forming your squad, ensure a good balance of different classes and abilities to cover various roles on the battlefield. Experiment with different combinations and adapt your squad composition based on the objectives and challenges you face during each encounter.
A Medic for example who is versed in BIOChemistry to make sure your squad does get out of it alive is a great pick.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/8c94ff169d0dfc767985bfed78bd0caab50f69d5.png[/img]

[h1]#2 Analyze the Environment[/h1]

The game features diverse maps and environments, each with its own advantages and challenges. Take the time to familiarize yourself with the maps, and study key locations, chokepoints, and objective areas. Understanding the layout will allow you to plan strategies, find advantageous positions, and anticipate enemy movements.
The Pull/Push of objects will become your biggest friend.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/d7af91ce0aaa0c638af639b2fbfb3a20ab89cb70.png[/img]

[h1]#3 Loot, Upgrade, Craft[/h1]

USC: Counterforce incorporates elements of looting, upgrading, and crafting.
Throughout the game, you'll find resources, weapons, and equipment.
Collect these items and utilize the crafting system to upgrade your gear, enhance your abilities, and gain an edge over your opponents. Pay attention to resource management and make strategic decisions on how to allocate your resources effectively.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/418c552ef269611bd4f0937b915b3068c3be02c4.png[/img]

[h1]#4 Combos & Buildups[/h1]

Mastering the combat mechanics and understanding the synergy between different abilities and weapons is crucial.
Experiment with different combos and buildups to maximize your damage output and tactical advantage. Discover how certain abilities and weapons can complement each other, creating devastating combinations that can turn the tide of battle in your favour.
For example, you can use a cryo weapon to build up enough frost to freeze a target and shatter/instakill it with a high-impact attack.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/931854b0695759072f357e1e994080a391cba217.png[/img]

[h1]#5 Encyclopedia/Wiki[/h1]

To deepen your understanding of USC: Counterforce, make use of the available resources like the in-game encyclopedia or [url=http://uscthegame.com/]an external wiki[/url].
These resources provide detailed information about the game mechanics, classes, weapons, abilities, and strategies. Refer to them to gain insights, learn advanced tactics, and stay updated on any balance changes or updates to the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41306942/c4d01bac1e361c9465ce52eaa27c11ca1f991c71.png[/img]

Now, you're (almost) all prepared! With these tips, you are no longer a rookie. Training will empower your strategic prowess and prepare you for the challenges ahead. The aliens are many, fierce and relentless. You fall and rise again and learn from your mistakes until you manage to save humanity from this alien threat.

Gear up and get ready to [b]join the USC[/b] for this mission [b]now in Early Access on Steam[/b]!

The USC: Counterforce team
